question: What is the foremost duty of Allah's servants?
answer: The foremost duty of Allah's servants is to know the purpose for which Allah created them and regarding which He took a promise from them; to know why He sent His messengers to them and why He revealed His Scriptures to them; to know the reason for the creation of this world, the Hereafter, Paradise, and Hell; and due to what the Inevitable Event (al-Haqqah) will come, the Day of Resurrection will occur, the Scales will be set up, the records of deeds will be scattered, and it will become clear that some were successful while others were doomed; and finally, to know the purpose for which light is apportioned. Allah the Almighty said: 'And he for whom Allah has not appointed light, for him there is no light.'
short_answer: Knowing the purpose of creation, the mission of the messengers, the Day of Judgment, and the Light of Allah.

question: For what purpose was all existence created?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'We did not create the heavens and earth and what is between them in play. We did not create them except in truth, but most of them do not know.' (Ad-Dukhan, 38-39). 'And We did not create the heaven and earth and that between them aimlessly. That is the assumption of those who disbelieve...' (Sad, 27). 'And Allah created the heavens and earth in truth and so that every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged.' (Al-Jathiyah, 22). Allah the Almighty also said: 'And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me.'
short_answer: For truth and to worship Allah.

question: What does the word 'slave' ('abd') mean?
answer: If 'slave' is understood as one who is subjugated, i.e., subdued and submissive, then in this sense the term 'slave' applies to all created beings in the higher or lower realms, whether rational or irrational, wet or dry, moving or stationary, apparent or hidden, believer or disbeliever, righteous or wicked, and so on. All this belongs to Allah the Almighty and Majestic, is subject to Him, subdued by Him, and managed by Him. All of the aforementioned follows what is prescribed for it, everything has its limit which it will reach, and its term which it will not exceed for an instant. 'Such is the determination of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.' (Ya-Sin, 38) and such are the results of the management of the Just, the Wise. If by the word 'slave' (abd) one means a worshipper ('abid), loving and obedient, then this pertains only to the believers, who are those honored servants of His and the God-fearing creatures close to Him, who will have no fear nor will they grieve.
short_answer: 1. Subjugated creation (all beings). 2. Worshipper (believers).

question: What is worship ('ibadah)? When does an action become worship?
answer: Worship refers to all apparent and hidden words and deeds that Allah loves and is pleased with, on one hand, and dissociation from everything incompatible with and contrary to such words and deeds, on the other. An action becomes worship when two things are perfected in that action: love and submission. Allah the Almighty said: '...but those who have believed are stronger in love for Allah.' (Al-Baqarah, 165). Allah the Almighty also said: 'Indeed, they who are apprehensive from fear of their Lord...' (Al-Mu'minun, 57). And Allah the Almighty combined the first and the second, saying: 'Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds and supplicate Us in hope and fear, and they were to Us humbly submissive.' (Al-Anbiya, 90).
short_answer: Deeds loved by Allah. Becomes worship with love and submission.

question: What is the sign of a servant's love for his Almighty and Majestic Lord?
answer: The sign of this is the servant's love for what Allah loves and his hatred for what angers Him. Furthermore, a sign of such love is that the servant fulfills Allah's commands, avoids what He has prohibited, and shows affection to those close to Him. This is why love and hate for the sake of Allah most securely connect a person to faith, as indicated by the noble hadith in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, reported from Al-Bara' bin 'Azib, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah, ﷺ, said: 'The strongest bond of faith is love for the sake of Allah and hatred for the sake of Allah.'
short_answer: Love for what Allah loves and hatred for what He hates.

question: How did Allah's servants come to know what He loves and what is pleasing to Him?
answer: They came to know this because Allah the Almighty sent His messengers to them and revealed His Scriptures, commanding them to do what He loves and is pleased with, and prohibiting what He does not love and rejects. This enabled them to know His irrefutable proofs and unparalleled wisdom. Allah the Almighty said: '[We sent] messengers as bringers of good tidings and warners so that mankind will have no argument against Allah after the messengers.' (An-Nisa, 165). Allah the Almighty also said: 'Say, [O Muhammad], "If you should love Allah, then follow me, [so] Allah will love you and forgive you your sins. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful."' (Ali 'Imran, 31).
short_answer: Through the messengers and the Scriptures.

question: How many conditions are there for worship?
answer: There are three conditions for worship: 1 - Sincere resolve, the presence of which is a necessary condition for the performance of worship itself. 2 - Sincerity of intention (Ikhlas). 3 - Conformity of any form of worship to the Shari'ah (Islamic law), for Allah the Almighty has commanded to practice religion only in accordance with the Shari'ah. Thus, worship will be accepted only if the intention is sincere and the worship conforms to the Shari'ah.
short_answer: Three conditions: resolve, sincerity, conformity to the Shari'ah.

question: What is sincere resolve?
answer: It is abandoning laziness and negligence and a person's effort to confirm his words with action. Allah the Almighty said: 'O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do? Great is hatred in the sight of Allah that you say what you do not do.' (As-Saff, 2-3).
short_answer: Abandoning laziness and confirming words with deeds.

question: What does sincerity of intention mean?
answer: The sincerity of a servant's intentions is evidenced by his aim in all his apparent and hidden words and deeds becoming the pursuit of the Countenance of Allah the Almighty. Allah the Almighty said: 'And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, [being] sincere to Him in religion, inclining to truth...' (Al-Bayyinah, 5). 'Who gives [from] his wealth to purify himself. And not [giving] for anyone who has [done him] a favor to be rewarded. But only seeking the countenance of his Lord, Most High.' (Al-Layl, 18-20). 'And they give food in spite of love for it to the needy, the orphan, and the captive, [Saying], "We feed you only for the countenance of Allah. We wish not from you reward or gratitude."' (Al-Insan, 8-9). Allah the Almighty also said: 'Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter - We increase for him in his harvest. And whoever desires the harvest of this world - We give him thereof, but there is not for him in the Hereafter any share.' (Ash-Shura, 20).
short_answer: Seeking the Countenance of Allah in all deeds.

question: What is meant by the religious law (Shari'ah) in strict accordance with which Allah the Almighty has commanded to practice the religion?
answer: This refers to the practice of pure monotheism, the religion of Ibrahim, peace be upon him. Allah the Almighty said: 'Indeed, the religion in the sight of Allah is Islam.' (Ali 'Imran, 19). 'Do they seek other than the religion of Allah while to Him have submitted [all] those within the heavens and earth, willingly or by compulsion?' (Ali 'Imran, 83). 'And who would be averse to the religion of Abraham except one who makes a fool of himself?' (Al-Baqarah, 130). 'And whoever desires other than Islam as religion - never will it be accepted from him, and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers.' (Ali 'Imran, 85). Allah the Almighty also said: 'Or have they other deities who have ordained for them a religion to which Allah has not consented?' (Ash-Shura, 21). There are other verses indicating this.
short_answer: Practicing Monotheism (Islam), the religion of Ibrahim.

question: How many levels does Islam comprise?
answer: Three levels: Islam (submission), Iman (faith), and Ihsan (excellence in worship), and each of these names can apply to the entire religion as a whole.
short_answer: Three levels: Islam, Iman, Ihsan.

question: What is 'Islam' (submission)?
answer: Islam is the expression of submission to Allah through monotheism, the manifestation of obedience to Him by fulfilling specific religious obligations, and absolute dissociation from polytheism. Allah the Almighty said: 'And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to Allah...?' (An-Nisa, 125). 'And whoever submits his face to Allah while he is a doer of good has certainly grasped the most trustworthy handhold.' (Luqman, 22). Allah the Almighty also said: 'So your God is One God, so submit to Him. And give good tidings to the humble [before their Lord].' (Al-Hajj, 34).
short_answer: Submission to Allah through Monotheism, obedience, and rejection of Shirk.

question: What indicates that the term 'Islam' encompasses the entire religion?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'Indeed, the religion in the sight of Allah is Islam.' (Ali 'Imran, 19). As for the Prophet, ﷺ, it is reported that he said: 'Islam began as something strange and will return as something strange as it began.' It is also reported that the Prophet, ﷺ, said: 'The best of Islam is to testify that there is no god but Allah.' (Ahmad (part of a longer hadith)).
short_answer: The words of Allah and the Prophet naming the entire religion Islam.

question: What evidence indicates that Islam can be defined by enumerating its five pillars?
answer: Evidence for this is found in the Prophet's words, ﷺ, in the hadith concerning Jibril's question about religion, to which the Messenger of Allah, ﷺ, replied: 'Islam is to testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, ﷺ, to establish prayer, to give Zakat, to fast in Ramadan, and to perform Hajj to the House (of Allah) if you are able to find a way (to do so).' (Muslim, Al-Bukhari, Abu Dawud, Ibn Majah, and An-Nasa'i (part of a longer hadith)). Further evidence is the Prophet's words, ﷺ, 'Islam is built upon five pillars...', after which he enumerated all the above, the only difference being the order of Hajj and fasting. Both hadiths are in the Sahih collections of Al-Bukhari and Muslim.
short_answer: Hadith of Jibril and the hadith on the five pillars of Islam.

question: What is the place of the two testimonies in the religion?
answer: A servant can only begin practicing the religion after uttering the words of these testimonies. Allah the Almighty said: 'The believers are only those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger.' (An-Nur, 62; Al-Hujurat, 15). Many other verses and hadiths confirm this.
short_answer: It is the condition for entering the religion.

question: What indicates the necessity of testifying that there is no god but Allah?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'Allah witnesses that there is no deity except Him, and [so do] the angels and those of knowledge - [that He is] maintaining [creation] in justice. There is no deity except Him, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.' (Ali 'Imran, 18). 'So know, [O Muhammad], that there is no deity except Allah...' (Muhammad, 19). 'And there is no deity except Allah...' (Ali 'Imran, 62). 'Allah has not taken any son, nor has there ever been with Him any deity...' (Al-Mu'minun, 91). Allah the Almighty also said: 'Say, [O Muhammad], "If there had been with Him [other] gods, as they say, then they [each] would have sought to the Owner of the Throne a way."' (Al-Isra, 42). Other verses could be cited confirming this.
short_answer: Numerous Quranic verses affirming the oneness of Allah.

question: What is the meaning of testifying that there is no god but Allah?
answer: The meaning of this testimony is the negation of anyone besides Allah being deserving of worship, and the affirmation that only Allah deserves it, having no partner in worship, just as He has no partner in His exclusive sovereignty. Allah the Almighty said: 'That is because Allah is the Truth, and that which they call upon other than Him is falsehood, and because Allah is the Most High, the Grand.' (Al-Hajj, 62).
short_answer: Negating false deities and affirming worship for Allah alone.

question: What are the conditions for the validity of the testimony that there is no god but Allah, without the full observance of which it will not benefit the one who utters it?
answer: There are seven such conditions: 1 - Knowledge of the meaning of what one negates and affirms when giving this testimony. 2 - Certainty of the heart in its truth. 3 - External and internal submission to it. 4 - Acceptance such that one does not reject any part of it, nor anything consistent with its meaning. 5 - Sincerity when uttering the words of the testimony. 6 - Truthfulness, manifest not only in words but emanating from the depths of the heart. 7 - Love for this testimony and for those who have uttered it. The meaning of these seven conditions is explained in more detail in the following eight questions.
short_answer: Seven conditions: Knowledge, Certainty, Submission, Acceptance, Sincerity, Truthfulness, Love.

question: Which Quranic verses and hadiths indicate the necessity of knowledge?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'Except those [angels] who testify to the truth while they know.' (Az-Zukhruf, 86). Here, 'testify to the truth' means they testify that there is no god but Allah, while holding in their hearts knowledge of the meaning of what their tongues utter. As for the Prophet, ﷺ, it is reported that he said: 'Whoever dies knowing that there is no god but Allah will enter Paradise.' (Muslim, Imam Ahmad). Both narrators transmit this hadith from 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him. At first glance, it might seem that only the heart's knowledge benefits a person, without the need to utter the two testimonies aloud or perform actions with body parts. However, a number of other hadiths clarify the meaning of this hadith as a whole, leading to the conclusion that our righteous predecessors did not take it literally, as they sought to reconcile the meanings of various Quranic verses and hadiths. Thus, faith in the understanding of the People of the Sunnah and the Community (Ahl as-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah) is verbal affirmation, conviction of the heart, and performance of actions corresponding to the five pillars of Islam.
short_answer: Verse (Az-Zukhruf, 86) and the hadith of 'Uthman about knowledge.

question: Which Quranic verses and hadiths indicate the necessity of certainty?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'The believers are only those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and then doubt not but strive with their properties and their lives in the cause of Allah. It is those who are the truthful.' (Al-Hujurat, 15). As for the Prophet, ﷺ, it is reported that he said: 'I testify that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah. Any servant who meets Allah with these two testimonies, without doubting their truth, will certainly enter Paradise.' (Muslim). It is also reported that the Prophet, ﷺ, once said to Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him: 'Give glad tidings of Paradise to anyone you meet behind this wall who testifies that there is no god but Allah, being certain of it in his heart.'
short_answer: Verse (Al-Hujurat, 15) and hadiths about the absence of doubt.

question: Which Quranic verses indicate the necessity of submission to Allah's will?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'And whoever submits his face to Allah while he is a doer of good has certainly grasped the most trustworthy handhold.' (Luqman, 22). Allah the Almighty also said: 'But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you, [O Muhammad], judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves and then find within themselves no discomfort from what you have judged and submit in [full, willing] submission.' (An-Nisa, 65).
short_answer: Verses about submission to Allah and acceptance of His rulings.

question: Which Quranic verses and hadiths indicate the necessity of internal acceptance (heartfelt agreement) with the words of the testimony?
answer: Regarding those who did not accept the words of the testimony, Allah the Almighty said: '[And it will be said], "Assemble those who wronged and their kinds and what they used to worship other than Allah, and guide them to the path of Hellfire. And stop them; indeed, they are to be questioned. Why do you not help each other?" But they, that Day, are in surrender. And they will approach one another, inquiring of each other. They will say, "Indeed, you used to come at us from the right." They will reply, "Rather, you [yourselves] were not believers, and we had over you no authority. Rather, you were a transgressing people. So the word of our Lord has come into effect upon us; indeed, we will taste [punishment]. And we led you to deviation; indeed, we ourselves were deviators." So indeed they, that Day, will be sharing in the punishment. Indeed, that is how We deal with the criminals. Indeed, when it was said to them, "There is no deity but Allah," they were arrogant and said, "Should we leave our gods for a mad poet?"' (As-Saffat, 22-36). As for the Prophet, ﷺ, it is reported that he said: 'The guidance and knowledge with which Allah has sent me is like abundant rain that fell on some land. A part of the land was fertile: it absorbed the water and brought forth much grass and herbage. Another part was hard: it held the water, and Allah benefited people by it, who drank, gave others to drink, and irrigated. Another part was barren: it could neither hold water nor bring forth herbage. (These types of land) are like those who understand the religion of Allah, benefit from that with which Allah sent me, acquire knowledge and teach it; and those who do not turn to it themselves nor accept the guidance of Allah with which I was sent.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim).
short_answer: Verses about the arrogance of disbelievers and the hadith about land and rain.

question: Which Quranic verses and hadiths indicate the necessity of sincerity (Ikhlas)?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'Unquestionably, for Allah is the pure religion.' (Az-Zumar, 3). Allah the Almighty also said: 'So worship Allah, [being] sincere to Him in religion.' (Az-Zumar, 2). As for the Prophet, ﷺ, it is reported that he said: 'The people who will be happiest with my intercession are those who said, "La ilaha illa-llah" (None has the right to be worshipped but Allah) sincerely from the heart.' (Al-Bukhari, Imam Ahmad). It is also reported that the Prophet, ﷺ, said: 'Indeed, Allah has forbidden the Fire from touching anyone who says "La ilaha illa-llah" seeking thereby the Countenance of Allah.' (Al-Bukhari).
short_answer: Verses and hadiths about sincere worship for Allah alone.

question: What evidence in the Quran and Sunnah indicates the necessity of truthfulness?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'Alif, Lam, Meem. Do the people think that they will be left to say, "We believe" and they will not be tried? But We have certainly tried those before them, and Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful, and He will surely make evident the liars.' (Al-Ankabut, 1-3). As for the Prophet, ﷺ, it is reported that he said: 'Whoever testifies that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, with truthfulness in his heart, Allah will certainly forbid the Fire from touching him.' (Al-Bukhari). It is also reported that once the Prophet, ﷺ, was instructing a Bedouin about the Shari'ah, and when he finished, the Bedouin said, 'By Allah, I will neither add to this nor omit from it.' Thereupon the Messenger of Allah, ﷺ, said: 'He will be successful if he is truthful.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim).
short_answer: Verses and hadiths about truthfulness (Sidq) in faith.

question: Which Quranic verses and hadiths indicate the necessity of love?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'O you who have believed, whoever of you should revert from his religion - Allah will bring forth [in place of them] a people He will love and who will love Him...' (Al-Ma'idah, 54). As for the Prophet, ﷺ, it is reported that he said: 'Whoever possesses three (qualities) will taste the sweetness of faith: that he loves Allah and His Messenger more than anything else; that he loves a person only for the sake of Allah; and that he would hate to revert to disbelief after Allah has saved him from it, as he would hate to be thrown into the Fire.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim).
short_answer: Verses and hadiths about love for Allah and His Messenger.

question: What indicates the necessity of showing allegiance and enmity for the sake of Allah?
answer: Allah the Almighty and Majestic said: 'Your ally is none but Allah and [therefore] His Messenger and those who have believed - those who establish prayer and give Zakah, and they bow [in worship].' (Al-Ma'idah, 55). 'You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day having affection for those who oppose Allah and His Messenger...' (Al-Mujadilah, 22). Allah the Almighty also said: 'O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies...' (Al-Mumtahanah, 1). And all the verses of Surah Al-Mumtahanah speak of this.
short_answer: Verses about allegiance and enmity for the sake of Allah (Al-Wala' wal-Bara').

question: What indicates the necessity of testifying that Muhammad, ﷺ, is the Messenger of Allah?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'Certainly did Allah confer [great] favor upon the believers when He sent among them a Messenger from themselves, reciting to them His verses and purifying them and teaching them the Book and wisdom, although they had been before in manifest error.' (Ali 'Imran, 164). 'There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves. Grievous to him is what you suffer; [he is] concerned over you [i.e., your guidance] and to the believers is kind and merciful.' (At-Tawbah, 128). Allah the Almighty also said: 'And Allah knows that you are His Messenger...' (Al-Munafiqun, 1). Other verses indicating this can be cited.
short_answer: Verses confirming the mission of Muhammad ﷺ.

question: What is the meaning of testifying that Muhammad, ﷺ, is the Messenger of Allah?
answer: Such testimony implies heartfelt confirmation of the statement that Muhammad is the servant and messenger of Allah to all mankind and jinn, about whom Allah the Almighty says: '...as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner and one who invites to Allah, by His permission, and a lamp spreading light.' (See: Al-Ahzab, 45-46). One must believe in everything he reported about the past and the future, what is lawful and what is prohibited, and one must obey his commands and refrain from what he forbade, adhere to his Shari'ah, and steadfastly follow his Sunnah privately and publicly, agreeing with his judgment and submitting to it. One must also believe that obeying him is obeying Allah, and disobeying him is disobeying Allah, for he conveyed His message to the people. Allah only took him after He perfected this religion through His Messenger and after this Messenger clearly conveyed everything he was entrusted with, leaving his community upon a clear path from which only the utterly lost can deviate after that. Many other related issues will be discussed later, if Allah wills.
short_answer: Belief in his messengership, obedience, and following the Sunnah.

question: What are the necessary conditions for testifying that Muhammad, ﷺ, is the Messenger of Allah, and will the first part of the testimony be accepted without this?
answer: We have previously stated that a servant of Allah cannot begin practicing the religion without giving these two testimonies, and that they are interconnected. Thus, the conditions of the first testimony are also the conditions of the second, and the conditions of the second are the conditions of the first.
short_answer: The same conditions as for the first testimony (interconnectedness).

question: What indicates the necessity of prayer and paying Zakat?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'And if they repent, establish prayer, and give Zakah, then let them go on their way...' (At-Tawbah, 5). 'And if they repent, establish prayer, and give Zakah, then they are your brothers in religion...' (At-Tawbah, 11). Allah the Almighty also said: 'And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, [being] sincere to Him in religion, inclining to truth, and to establish prayer and give Zakah...' (Al-Bayyinah, 5). Many other verses also indicate the necessity of prayer and paying Zakat.
short_answer: Quranic verses prescribing Salah and Zakat.

question: What indicates the necessity of fasting?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'O you who have believed, decreed upon you is fasting as it was decreed upon those before you...' (Al-Baqarah, 183). Allah the Almighty also said: 'So whoever sights [the new moon of] the month, let him fast it...' (Al-Baqarah, 185). In the hadith where the Prophet, ﷺ, instructed a Bedouin about the Shari'ah, it is reported that the Bedouin said, 'Tell me what Allah has made obligatory for me regarding fasting?' The Messenger of Allah, ﷺ, said: '(Fasting during) the month of Ramadan, unless you wish to fast some additional days voluntarily.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim).
short_answer: Verses on the prescription of fasting and the hadith about Ramadan.

question: What indicates the necessity of performing Hajj?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'And complete the Hajj and 'umrah for Allah.' (Al-Baqarah, 196). Allah the Almighty also said: 'And [due] to Allah from the people is a pilgrimage to the House - for whoever is able to find thereto a way...' (Ali 'Imran, 97). As for evidence from the Sunnah, it is reported that Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: 'The Messenger of Allah, ﷺ, addressed us and said, "O people! Allah has made Hajj obligatory upon you, so perform Hajj..."' (Muslim, Ahmad). We previously cited the hadith of Jibril and the hadith in which the Prophet, ﷺ, said: 'Islam is built upon five pillars...' Many similar examples could be given.
short_answer: Verses about the obligation of Hajj and the Prophet's call.

question: What is faith (Iman)?
answer: Faith is speech and action. This refers to words spoken by the heart and tongue, and actions performed by the heart, tongue, and other body parts. Faith increases through acts of obedience and decreases due to acts of disobedience, and in this regard, some believers can surpass others.
short_answer: Speech and action. It increases and decreases.

question: What evidence indicates that faith is a combination of speech and action?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: '...but Allah has endeared faith to you and has made it pleasing in your hearts...' (Al-Hujurat, 7). 'And believe in Allah and His Messenger...' (Al-A'raf, 168). This is the meaning of giving the two testimonies, for without it, a servant cannot begin practicing the religion. Regarding certain beliefs, these testimonies relate to actions of the heart; on the other hand, they relate to actions of the tongue expressing these beliefs, and they can only benefit the person giving them if there is agreement between the heart and tongue. Allah the Almighty also said: 'And Allah would not let your faith [i.e., prayer] be lost...' (Al-Baqarah, 143). Here, 'faith' refers to the prayers Muslims performed facing Bayt al-Maqdis before the change of the Qiblah. Thus, prayer in general was called faith in the sense that it combines actions of the heart, tongue, and other body parts. As for the Prophet, ﷺ, he attributed to faith the performance of prayers and other acts of worship on the Night of Decree, fasting and night prayers during Ramadan, and the five daily obligatory prayers. When the Prophet, ﷺ, was asked, 'Which deed is best?' he replied: 'Faith in Allah and His Messenger.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim).
short_answer: Verses about faith in the heart and actions (prayer is called faith).

question: What indicates the possibility of faith increasing and decreasing?
answer: Evidence for this includes the following words of the Almighty: '...that He may increase them in faith upon their faith...' (Al-Fath, 4). '...and We increased them in guidance.' (Al-Kahf, 13). 'And Allah increases those who were guided, in guidance...' (Maryam, 76). 'And He increases the rightly guided in guidance...' (Muhammad, 17). '...and to increase the faith of those who have believed...' (Al-Muddaththir, 31). 'But it has increased them in faith...' (At-Tawbah, 124). '...those to whom people [i.e., hypocrites] said, "Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them." But it [merely] increased them in faith...' (Ali 'Imran, 173). 'It did not increase them except in faith and submission.' (Al-Ahzab, 22). Other verses could be cited as evidence. As for the Prophet, ﷺ, it is reported that he once said to his companions: 'If you were always in the state you are in when with me and constantly remembered (Allah), the angels would shake hands with you.' (Muslim).
short_answer: Numerous verses about the increase of faith and guidance.
source: Al-Fath, 4; Al-Kahf, 13; Maryam, 76; Muhammad, 17; At-Tawbah, 124; Ali 'Imran, 173; Al-Ahzab, 22; Muslim

question: What indicates that believers can surpass one another in their faith?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'And the forerunners, the forerunners - those are the ones brought near [to Allah] in the Gardens of Pleasure... Many of the first [to believe] and few of the last. [They are] on thrones woven [with ornament], reclining on them, facing each other. There will circulate among them young boys made eternal. With vessels, pitchers and a cup [of wine] from a flowing spring - no headache will they have therefrom, nor will they be intoxicated - and fruit of what they select and the meat of fowl, from whatever they desire. And [for them are] fair women with large, [beautiful] eyes, the likenesses of pearls well-protected, as reward for what they used to do. They will not hear therein any ill speech - only [greetings of] "Peace! Peace!" And the companions of the right - what are the companions of the right?' (Al-Waqi'ah, 10-27). Allah the Almighty also said: 'But if he is of those brought near, then [for him is] rest and bounty and a garden of pleasure. And if he is of the companions of the right, then [the angels will say], "Peace for you from the companions of the right."' (Al-Waqi'ah, 88-91). Allah the Almighty also said: 'Then We caused to inherit the Book those We have chosen of Our servants; and among them is he who wrongs himself, and among them is he who is moderate, and among them is he who is foremost in good deeds by permission of Allah...' (Fatir, 32). In the hadith on intercession, it is reported that the Prophet, ﷺ, said: 'There will come out of Hell-Fire anyone who said, "La ilaha illa-llah," having a grain of barley of good in his heart; then there will come out of Hell-Fire anyone who said, "La ilaha illa-llah," having a grain of wheat of good in his heart; then there will come out of Hell-Fire anyone who said, "La ilaha illa-llah," having an atom's weight of good in his heart.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim).
short_answer: Verses about degrees (the forerunners, companions of the right) and the hadith about the weight of faith.

question: What indicates that the concept of "faith" can encompass the entire religion as a whole?
answer: In the hadith about the Prophet's, ﷺ, conversation with the delegation of the tribe of 'Abd al-Qays, it is reported that he said: 'I command you to believe in Allah alone,' and he asked: 'Do you know what belief in Allah alone means?' They replied, 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' Then he said: 'It is to testify that none has the right to be worshipped but Allah alone, and that Muhammad is Allah's Messenger, to establish prayer, to pay Zakat, to fast in Ramadan, and to give one-fifth of the war booty.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim).
short_answer: Hadith where the Prophet included the deeds of Islam in the concept of Faith.

question: What evidence indicates that faith can be precisely defined by enumerating its six pillars?
answer: Evidence for this is the Prophet's words, ﷺ, in response to Jibril's question, peace be upon him: 'Tell me about faith.' He replied: '[It is] to believe in Allah, His angels, His Books, His Messengers, the Last Day, and to believe in divine destiny (qadar), both the good and the bad thereof.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim).
short_answer: Hadith of Jibril about the six pillars of Iman (Faith).

question: What evidence in the Quran indicates the existence of the aforementioned pillars of faith in general?
answer: Allah the Almighty said: 'Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the east or the west, but [true] righteousness is [in] one who believes in Allah, the Last Day, the angels, the Book, and the prophets...' (Al-Baqarah, 177). Allah the Almighty also said: 'Indeed, all things We created with predestination.' (Al-Qamar, 49). If Allah wills, we will discuss each of these pillars separately below.
short_answer: Verse 177 of Surah Al-Baqarah and verse 49 of Surah Al-Qamar.

question: What does belief in Allah the Almighty and Majestic mean?
answer: It is the heartfelt confirmation of the existence of Allah the Almighty, whom nothing preceded and nothing will succeed, that He is the First, before whom there was nothing, and He is the Last, after whom there will be nothing, that He is the Evident (Az-Zahir), above whom there is nothing, and He is the Hidden (Al-Batin), beyond whom there is nothing, and He is the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence, the One, the Eternal. Allah the Almighty said: 'He neither begets nor is born, nor is there to Him any equivalent.' (Al-Ikhlas, 3-4). And belief in Allah implies the recognition that He alone is the Deity and Lord and that He alone possesses the names and attributes that are uniquely His.
short_answer: Belief in His existence, eternity, and oneness.

question: What does the recognition of Allah as the only deity (Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah) mean?
answer: Such recognition implies dedicating all types of apparent and hidden worship, expressed in words and deeds, solely to Allah the Almighty and Majestic, on one hand, and negating the permissibility of worshipping anything other than Allah the Most High, on the other, as the Most High said: 'And your Lord has decreed that you worship not except Him.' (Al-Isra, 23). 'And worship Allah and associate nothing with Him...' (An-Nisa, 36). Allah the Most High also said: 'Indeed, I am Allah. There is no deity except Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance.' (Ta-Ha, 14). The same idea is expressed in many other verses. This recognition is what puts the testimony that there is no god but Allah into practice.
short_answer: Worshipping Allah alone and rejecting worship to others.

question: What is the opposite of recognizing Allah as the only deity?
answer: The opposite of this is Shirk (associating partners with Allah), which is of two types: Major Shirk and Minor Shirk. Major Shirk completely nullifies the aforementioned recognition, while Minor Shirk negates its perfection.
short_answer: Polytheism (Shirk), which is divided into Major and Minor.

question: What is Major Shirk?
answer: Major Shirk is manifested when a servant chooses, alongside Allah, someone whom he begins to equate with the Lord of the worlds, loving them as he loves Allah, fearing them as he fears Allah, seeking refuge in them, supplicating to them, being in awe of them, asking them for things, striving towards them, relying on them, or obeying them while abandoning obedience to Allah, or following them in what displeases Allah, or doing similar things. Allah the Most High said: 'Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And he who associates others with Allah has certainly fabricated a tremendous sin.' (An-Nisa, 48). '...and whoever associates others with Allah has certainly gone far astray.' (An-Nisa, 116). 'Indeed, he who associates others with Allah - Allah has forbidden him Paradise, and his refuge is the Fire...' (Al-Ma'idah, 72). Allah the Most High also said: '...And whoever associates others with Allah - it is as though he had fallen from the sky and was snatched by the birds or the wind carried him down into a remote place.' (Al-Hajj, 31). Other verses could be cited in this regard. As for the Prophet, ﷺ, it is reported that he said: 'The right of Allah upon His servants is that they should worship Him (Alone) and should not worship anything besides Him, and the right of the servants upon Allah is that He should not punish anyone who worships none besides Him.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). Excluded from the religion are both those who openly commit Major Shirk, such as the disbelieving Quraysh and their like, and those who are hidden polytheists, such as the hypocrites who try to deceive Allah, professing Islam outwardly while being disbelievers inwardly. Allah the Most High said: 'Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire - and never will you find for them a helper - except for those who repent, correct themselves, hold fast to Allah, and are sincere in their religion for Allah. Those will be with the believers.' (An-Nisa, 145-146). Many other verses indicate this.
short_answer: Equating others with Allah in worship. It is unforgiven.

question: What is Minor Shirk?
answer: This is a measure of showing off (riya') that mixes with striving to do something properly for the sake of Allah the Most High. Allah the Most High said: 'So whoever would hope for the meeting with his Lord - let him do righteous work and not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone.' (Al-Kahf, 110). As for the Messenger of Allah, ﷺ, he once said: 'Indeed, what I fear most for you is Minor Shirk.' They asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, what is Minor Shirk?' He replied: 'Showing off (riya').' (Ahmad, Al-Baghawi, Al-Haythami). Later, the Prophet, ﷺ, explained his words: '(It means that) a person will stand for prayer and beautify it when he sees someone looking at him.' (Part of a hadith reported by Ahmad and Ibn Majah). This also includes cases where oaths are sworn by other than Allah, such as by parents, idols, the Ka'bah, one's trustworthiness, or anything else. It is reported that the Prophet, ﷺ, said: 'Do not swear by your fathers, nor by your mothers, nor by idols.' (Abu Dawud). It is also reported that the Prophet, ﷺ, said: 'Whoever swears an oath, let him swear by the Lord of the Ka'bah.' (An-Nasa'i, Ahmad). It is also reported that the Prophet, ﷺ, said: 'Do not swear by anything besides Allah.' (Abu Dawud, An-Nasa'i). It is also reported that the Prophet, ﷺ, said: 'Whoever swears by his trustworthiness is not from us.' (Abu Dawud). It is also reported that the Prophet, ﷺ, said: 'Whoever swears by other than Allah has committed disbelief (or: ...polytheism).' (Abu Dawud). The same applies to saying phrases like: 'What Allah wills and you will.' It is reported that in response to a man who once said this to him, the Prophet, ﷺ, said: 'Have you made me an equal to Allah? (You should say): 'What Allah alone wills!'' (Al-Bukhari, Ibn Majah, Ahmad). The same applies to expressions like: 'If it weren't for Allah and you,' and 'I have no one except Allah and you,' and 'I seek refuge with Allah and you,' and similar phrases. It is reported that the Prophet, ﷺ, said: 'Do not say: 'What Allah wills and so-and-so wills,' but say: 'What Allah wills, and then what so-and-so wills.'' (Abu Dawud, Ahmad). Scholars have stated that one may say: 'If it weren't for Allah, and then so-and-so,' but one should not say: 'If it weren't for Allah and so-and-so.'
short_answer: Showing off (Riya') and swearing oaths by other than Allah.

question: What is the difference between using the conjunction 'and' and the phrase 'and then' in the aforementioned expressions?
answer: The difference is that connecting two words with the conjunction 'and' requires juxtaposition and equation. Thus, a person who says, 'What Allah wills and you will,' juxtaposes the will of the servant with the will of Allah, equating one with the other. However, if the phrase 'and then' is used for connection, the situation changes, as it indicates belonging and dependence. This means that a person who says, 'What Allah wills, and then you will,' thereby affirms the fact that the servant's will is dependent on the will of Allah the Most High and that the servant's will is secondary, as indicated by the Most High who said: 'And you do not will except that Allah wills.' (Al-Insan, 30). The same applies to everything else.
short_answer: 'And' equates (impermissible), 'and then' subordinates (permissible).

question: What does the recognition of Allah as the only Lord (Tawhid al-Rububiyyah) mean?
answer: This refers to the firm conviction that Allah the Most High is the Lord, Sovereign, Creator, and Manager of all existence, who disposes of all affairs as He wills, who shares His authority with no one, who has no protector against humiliation, and that no one can repel His command, repeal His decree, or oppose Him. It is the belief that there is none like Him, none with similar names, and none who can compete with Him in any aspect related to His Lordship or consistent with His names and attributes. Allah the Most High said: '[All] praise is [due] to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darkness and the light...' (Al-An'am, 1). The same is discussed in the rest of the verses of this surah. '[All] praise is [due] to Allah, Lord of the worlds...' (Al-Fatihah, 1). 'Say, "Who is Lord of the heavens and earth?" Say, "Allah." Say, "Have you then taken besides Him allies not possessing [even] for themselves any benefit or any harm?" Say, "Is the blind equivalent to the seeing? Or is darkness equivalent to light? Or have they attributed to Allah partners who created like His creation so that the creation [of each] seemed similar to them?" Say, "Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the Prevailing."' (Ar-Ra'd, 16). 'It is Allah who created you, then provided for you, then will cause you to die, and then will give you life. Are there any of your 'partners' who does anything of that? Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him.' (Ar-Rum, 40). 'This is the creation of Allah. So show Me what those other than Him have created.' (Luqman, 11). 'Or were they created by nothing, or were they the creators [of themselves]? Or did they create the heavens and the earth? Rather, they are not certain.' (At-Tur, 35-36). '[He is] Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, so worship Him and have patience for His worship. Do you know of any similarity to Him?' (Maryam, 65). 'There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the Hearing, the Seeing.' (Ash-Shura, 11). 'And say, "[All] praise is [due] to Allah, who has not taken a son and has had no partner in [His] dominion and has no [need of a] protector out of weakness; and glorify Him with [great] glorification."' (Al-Isra, 111). Allah the Most High also said: 'Say, "Invoke those you have claimed [as deities] besides Allah." They do not possess an atom's weight [of ability] in the heavens or on the earth, and they do not have therein any partnership [with Him], nor is there for Him from among them any assistant. And intercession does not benefit with Him except for one whom He permits.' (Saba, 22-23).
short_answer: Certainty that only Allah creates, owns, and manages.
source: Al-An'am, 1; Al-Fatihah, 1; Ar-Ra'd, 16; Ar-Rum, 40; Luqman, 11; At-Tur, 35-36; Maryam, 65; Ash-Shura, 11; Al-Isra, 111; Saba, 22-23

question: What is the opposite of recognizing Allah as the only Lord?
answer: The opposite of this is the belief that alongside Allah, someone else can manage anything in the universe, creating or destroying, giving life or taking it, bringing benefit or repelling harm, and that this other is capable of doing something that is actually only within the power of the Lord. The same applies to the belief that someone can rival the Lord in matters consistent with the meaning of His names and attributes, such as knowledge of the unseen, greatness, and so on. Allah the Most High said: 'No one can withhold [the favors] Allah grants to people, nor can anyone release whatever He withholds. He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise. O people, remember the favor of Allah upon you. Is there any creator other than Allah who provides for you from the heaven and earth? There is no deity except Him, so how are you deluded?' (Fatir, 2-3). 'If Allah should afflict you with harm, there is no remover of it except Him. And if He intends for you good, then there is no repeller of His bounty...' (Yunus, 107). 'Say, "Have you considered: if the punishment of Allah should come to you or the Hour come to you - would you call upon other than Allah, if you should be truthful?" Rather, Him [alone] you call upon; and He will remove that for which you called upon Him if He wills, and you will forget what you associate [with Him].' (Al-An'am, 40-41). 'And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him.' (Al-An'am, 59). 'Say, "None in the heavens and earth knows the unseen except Allah..."' (An-Naml, 65). Allah the Most High also said: '...and they encompass not a thing of His knowledge except for what He wills...' (Al-Baqarah, 255). As for the Prophet, ﷺ, it is reported that he said: 'Allah the Most High says: 'Grandeur is My garment, and majesty is My lower garment. Whoever competes with Me regarding either of them, I will cast him into the Fire.'' (Muslim, Ahmad).
short_answer: Belief that someone other than Allah manages the universe.
source: Fatir, 2-3; Yunus, 107; Al-An'am, 40-41, 59; An-Naml, 65; Al-Baqarah, 255; Hadith (Muslim, Ahmad)

question: What is the meaning of the recognition that only Allah possesses specific names and attributes (Tawhid al-Asma' wa al-Sifat)?
answer: It is the belief in the Most Beautiful Names and the Lofty Attributes by which Allah the Most High has described Himself in His Book and by which His Messenger, ﷺ, has described Him. Such recognition implies using the aforementioned names and attributes exactly as they occur in the Quran and the Sunnah, and it precludes questioning about other possible meanings of these names. In other words, they should be used as Allah the Most High has used them, combining affirmation of the existence of these names and attributes with the denial of any permissibility of altering them, as indicated multiple times in the Quran. For example, the Most High said: 'They cannot encompass Him in knowledge.' (Ta-Ha, 110). 'There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the Hearing, the Seeing.' (Ash-Shura, 11). Allah the Most High also said: 'Vision perceives Him not, but He perceives [all] vision; and He is the Subtle, the Acquainted.' (Al-An'am, 103). At-Tirmidhi reports a hadith from Ubayy bin Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him, that when the Messenger of Allah, ﷺ, mentioned the gods of the polytheists, they said to him: 'Tell us about the lineage of your Lord.' Then Allah the Most High revealed the verses: 'Say, "He is Allah, [who is] One, Allah, the Eternal Refuge."' (Al-Ikhlas, 1-2). This means He is the Eternal in the sense that 'He neither begets nor is born' (Al-Ikhlas, 3), for any begotten being will inevitably die, and any mortal being necessarily leaves behind an heir. As for Allah the Most High, He does not die and leaves no one after Him, 'Nor is there to Him any equivalent.' (Al-Ikhlas, 4). With these last words, Allah indicated that there is nothing similar to Him, equal to Him, or like Him. (At-Tirmidhi).
short_answer: Belief in Allah's Names and Attributes without distortion or anthropomorphism.

question: What evidence in the Quran and Sunnah indicates the Most Beautiful Names of Allah?
answer: Allah the Most High said: 'And to Allah belong the best names, so invoke Him by them. And leave [the company of] those who practice deviation concerning His names...' (Al-A'raf, 180). 'Say, "Call upon Allah or call upon the Most Merciful. Whichever [name] you call - to Him belong the best names."' (Al-Isra, 110). Allah the Most High also said: 'Allah - there is no deity except Him. To Him belong the best names.' (Ta-Ha, 8). Other verses could be cited as examples. As for the Prophet, ﷺ, it is reported that he said: 'Indeed, Allah has ninety-nine names. Whoever enumerates them will enter Paradise.' It is also reported that when supplicating, the Prophet, ﷺ, would say: 'O Allah, I ask You by every name belonging to You which You have named Yourself with, or revealed in Your Book, or You taught to any of Your creation, or You have preserved in the knowledge of the unseen with You, that You make the Quran the life of my heart...' (Ahmad, Al-Hakim).
short_answer: Surah Al-A'raf, verse 180, and the hadith about the 99 names.

question: Which of the Most Beautiful Names are mentioned in the Quran?
answer: Allah the Most High said: 'Indeed, Allah is ever Exalted and Grand.' (An-Nisa, 34). 'Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle and Acquainted.' (Al-Ahzab, 34). '...indeed, He is Knowing and Competent.' (Fatir, 44). 'Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Seeing.' (An-Nisa, 58). 'Indeed, Allah is ever Exalted in Might and Wise.' (An-Nisa, 56). 'Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.' (An-Nisa, 23). '...indeed, He is to them Kind and Merciful.' (At-Tawbah, 117). '...and Allah is Free of need and Forbearing.' (Al-Baqarah, 263). 'Indeed, He is the Praiseworthy, the Glorious.' (Hud, 73). 'Indeed, my Lord is, over all things, Guardian.' (Hud, 57). '...indeed, Allah is ever, over you, an Observer.' (An-Nisa, 1). '...and sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.' (An-Nisa, 81). '...and sufficient is Allah as Accountant.' (An-Nisa, 6). 'Indeed, Allah is, over all things, a Keeper.' (An-Nisa, 85). '...your Lord, over all things, is Witness.' (Fussilat, 53). 'Allah - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence.' (Al-Baqarah, 255). 'He is the First and the Last, the Ascendant and the Intimate, and He is, of all things, Knowing.' (Al-Hadid, 3). Allah the Most High also said: 'He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed. He is the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, the Sovereign, the Pure, the Perfection, the Bestower of Faith, the Overseer, the Exalted in Might, the Compeller, the Superior. Exalted is Allah above whatever they associate with Him. He is Allah, the Creator, the Inventor, the Fashioner; to Him belong the best names...' (Al-Hashr, 22-24). Other verses could be cited as examples.
short_answer: Allah, Ar-Rahman, Al-Halim, Al-Hayy, and others.
source: An-Nisa, 1, 6, 23, 34, 56, 58, 81, 85; Al-Ahzab, 34; Fatir, 44; At-Tawbah, 117; Al-Baqarah, 263; Hud, 57, 73; Fussilat, 53; Al-Baqarah, 255; Al-Hadid, 3; Al-Hashr, 22-24

question: Which of the Most Beautiful Names are mentioned in the Sunnah?
answer: It is reported that when supplicating, the Prophet, ﷺ, would say: 'There is no god but Allah, the Forbearing, the Generous. There is no god but Allah, the Lord of the Magnificent Throne. There is no god but Allah, the Lord of the heavens and the earth, and the Lord of the Noble Throne.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). It is also reported that when supplicating, the Prophet, ﷺ, would say: 'O Creator of the heavens and the earth! O Possessor of majesty and honor! O Ever-Living, O Sustainer of existence!' (Ahmad, Al-Hakim). 'In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing can cause harm on earth or in heaven, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing.' (Ibn Majah, At-Tirmidhi). It is also reported that when supplicating, the Prophet, ﷺ, would say: 'O Allah, Knower of the unseen and the evident, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Lord and Sovereign of everything...' (At-Tirmidhi). It is also reported that when supplicating, the Prophet, ﷺ, would say: 'O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and the earth, our Lord and the Lord of everything, splitter of the grain and the date stone, Revealer of the Torah, the Gospel, and the Quran, I seek refuge with You from the evil of every evil creature that You grasp by the forelock! You are the First, and there is nothing before You; and You are the Last, and there is nothing after You; and You are the Ascendant, and there is nothing above You; and You are the Intimate, and there is nothing beyond You...' (Muslim, Ahmad). It is also reported that when supplicating, the Prophet, ﷺ, would say: 'O Allah, praise be to You, You are the light of the heavens and the earth and their inhabitants; praise be to You, You are the Sustainer of the heavens and the earth and their inhabitants.' (Al-Bukhari, Malik, Ahmad, Ad-Darimi). It is also reported that when supplicating, the Prophet, ﷺ, would say: 'O Allah, indeed I ask You, for I testify that You are Allah, there is no deity but You, the One, the Eternal Refuge, who neither begets nor is born, nor is there to Him any equivalent!' (At-Tirmidhi, Ahmad, Ad-Darimi, Abu Dawud). It is also reported that when supplicating, the Prophet, ﷺ, would say: 'O Turner of hearts!' (At-Tirmidhi, Ahmad, Ibn Majah). Many other similar examples could be cited.
short_answer: Names of Allah from the authentic supplications of the Prophet ﷺ.
source: Al-Bukhari, Muslim, Ahmad, At-Tirmidhi, Abu Dawud

question: Into how many types are the indications related to the Most Beautiful Names divided?
answer: Into three types: 1 - Indications related to the Essence of Allah. 2 - Indications to attributes that are derived from the Most Beautiful Names which encompass them. 3 - Indications to attributes that are not necessarily derived from the Most Beautiful Names.
short_answer: Three types: Essence, derived attributes, concomitant attributes.

question: What is an example of this?
answer: An example can be such names of the Most High as the Most Merciful (Ar-Rahman) and the Especially Merciful (Ar-Rahim), which indicate the Essence of the One to whom they belong, i.e., the Essence of Allah the Almighty and Majestic, and are applicable to Him. On the other hand, they indicate an attribute derived from these names which they encompass, i.e., mercy (rahmah), as well as a number of other attributes that are not derived from these names but are necessarily inherent in their Possessor, such as life and power. The same applies to all other names of Allah. The matter is different with created beings, for a person may be called wise while in reality he is ignorant, and similarly an unjust person may be called a just judge, a lowly person may be called mighty, a vile person may be called noble, a miser may be called generous, a bad person may be called righteous, and an unfortunate person may be called fortunate. As for Allah, glory and praise be to Him, He is exactly as He has characterized Himself, and He is above the descriptions given to Him by people.
short_answer: Example with the names the Most Merciful and the Especially Merciful.

question: Into how many parts are the indications of the Most Beautiful Names divided in terms of their content?
answer: They are divided into four parts: 1 - Allah is a comprehensive name that includes all the meanings of the Most Beautiful Names, which is why all other names are its attributes. For example, Allah the Most High said: 'He is Allah, the Creator, the Inventor, the Fashioner.' (Al-Hashr, 24). Other verses can be cited as examples. For the same reason, this name is never used as subordinate to other names. 2 - That which encompasses an essential attribute of Allah the Almighty and Majestic. An example is the name of the Most High, the Hearing (As-Sami'), which includes an indication of His hearing, through which He hears all sounds, and it makes no difference to Him whether they are secret or open. Another example is the name of Allah, the Seeing (Al-Basir), which includes an indication of His sight, which encompasses everything small and large that can be perceived by sight. A third example is the name of Allah, the Knowing (Al-'Alim), which encompasses His all-encompassing knowledge, about which Allah the Most High said: 'And not absent from your Lord is any [part] of an atom's weight within the earth or within the heaven or [anything] smaller than that or greater but that it is in a clear register.' (Saba, 3). As for the name of Allah, the All-Powerful (Al-Qadir), it includes an indication of His absolute power, by which He can create everything, destroy everything, etc. 3 - Names that contain indications of the attributes of Allah's actions, such as the Creator (Al-Khaliq), the Provider (Ar-Razzaq), the Inventor (Al-Bari'), the Fashioner (Al-Musawwir), etc. 4 - Names that contain indications that the Most High is free from any deficiencies, such as the Holy (Al-Quddus) and the Peace (As-Salam).
short_answer: Four parts: Name of Essence, attributes of essence, attributes of action, purification from deficiencies.

question: Into how many parts are the indications of the Most Beautiful Names divided in terms of their applicability to Allah the Almighty and Majestic?
answer: Among these names, there are those that can be applied to Allah either individually or in combination with other names. Specifically, these are names that contain any indications of attributes of perfection, such as the Living (Al-Hayy) and the Sustainer of existence (Al-Qayyum), the One (Al-Ahad) and the Eternal Refuge (As-Samad), etc. Among these names, there are also those applicable to Allah only together with other names that are their opposites, because using them alone might suggest that Allah has certain deficiencies. Examples include names such as the Bringer of Harm (Ad-Darr) and the Bringer of Benefit (An-Nafi'), the Humiliator (Al-Khafid) and the Exalter (Ar-Rafi'), the Giver (Al-Mu'ti) and the Withholder (Al-Mani'), the Honourer (Al-Mu'izz) and the Dishonourer (Al-Mudhill), etc. As for names such as the Bringer of Harm, the Humiliator, the Withholder, and the Dishonourer, it is not permissible to apply them to Allah individually, and they were not used in this way in the revelations, neither in the Quran nor in the Sunnah. Among such names is the name of the Most High, the Avenger (Al-Muntaqim), which is used in the Quran in combination with other related words, as in the words of the Most High: 'Indeed, We will take retribution upon the criminals.' (As-Sajdah, 22). Moreover, such names are used in cases where the word 'possessor' (Dhu) is used in combination with an attribute derived from such a name, as in the words of Allah the Most High: '...indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Owner of Retribution.' (Ali 'Imran, 4).
short_answer: Independent and paired (conjoined).

question: It was previously mentioned that among the attributes of Allah the Most High are essential attributes and attributes of action. What examples of essential attributes are found in the Quran and Sunnah?
answer: Allah the Most High said: 'But His hand is extended...' (Al-Ma'idah, 64). 'Everything will be destroyed except His Face.' (Al-Qasas, 88). 'But there will remain the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor.' (Ar-Rahman, 27). '...that you be brought up under My eye.' (Ta-Ha, 39). 'How excellent He is in seeing and hearing!' (Al-Kahf, 26). 'Indeed, I am with you, hearing and seeing.' (Ta-Ha, 46). 'They cannot encompass Him in knowledge.' (Ta-Ha, 110). '...and Allah spoke to Moses with [direct] speech.' (An-Nisa, 164). 'And when your Lord called Moses...' (Ash-Shu'ara, 10). 'And He called to them, "Did I not forbid you from that tree...?"' (Al-A'raf, 22). Allah the Most High also said: 'And [mention] the Day He will call them and say, "Where are My 'partners' which you used to claim?"' (Al-Qasas, 62). Corresponding examples exist in other verses. It is reported that the Prophet, ﷺ, said: 'His veil is light. If He were to remove it, the splendour of His Face would consume His creation as far as His sight reaches.' (Muslim). It is also reported that the Prophet, ﷺ, said: 'Allah's Hand is full, and its fullness is not diminished by continuous spending night and day. Do you see what He has spent since He created the heavens and the earth? Yet what is in His Hand has not decreased. His Throne is over the water, and in His other Hand is the balance (or: ...the grasp), and He raises and lowers.' (Muslim). In the hadith about the Dajjal, the Prophet, ﷺ, said: 'Indeed, Allah is not hidden from you; indeed, Allah is not one-eyed,' and saying this, he pointed with his hand to his eye. (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). It is also reported that when seeking help from Allah in a matter, the Prophet, ﷺ, would say: 'O Allah, I ask You by Your knowledge and by Your power, and I ask You of Your great bounty, for You are able and I am not, and You know and I do not know, and You are the Knower of the unseen.' It is also reported that the Prophet, ﷺ, said: 'You are not calling upon one deaf or absent. You are calling upon One Who is Hearing, Seeing, Near.' (Muslim, Ahmad, Al-Bukhari). In the hadith about the Resurrection, the Prophet, ﷺ, said: 'Allah the Most High will say: 'O Adam!' and he will respond: 'Here I am at Your service!'' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). A great many other hadiths are known in which it is reported that Allah will speak to His servants on the Day of Resurrection, and that He will speak to the inhabitants of Paradise, etc.
short_answer: Hands, Face, Eyes, Hearing, Sight, Knowledge, Speech.
source: Al-Ma'idah, 64; Al-Qasas, 88; Ta-Ha, 39; An-Nisa, 164; Hadiths (Al-Bukhari, Muslim)

question: What examples of attributes of action are found in the Quran?
answer: Allah the Most High said: 'It is He who created for you all of that which is on the earth. Then He directed Himself to the heaven...' (Al-Baqarah, 29). 'Do they await but that Allah should come to them in covers of clouds...?' (Al-Baqarah, 210). 'They have not appraised Allah with true appraisal, while the earth entirely will be [within] His grip on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand.' (Az-Zumar, 67). 'What prevented you from prostrating to that which I created with My hands?' (Sad, 75). 'And We wrote for him on the tablets [something] of all things...' (Al-A'raf, 145). 'And when his Lord appeared to the mountain, He rendered it level...' (Al-A'raf, 143). 'Indeed, Allah does what He wills.' (Al-Hajj, 18). Other verses could be cited as examples.
short_answer: Creation, Coming (Ityan), Grasping, Writing, Willing.

question: What examples of attributes of action are found in the Sunnah?
answer: It is reported that the Prophet, ﷺ, said: 'Our Lord descends to the lowest heaven every night when the last third of the night remains.' In the hadith about intercession, it is reported that the Prophet, ﷺ, said: 'Then Allah will come to them in a form they recognize and say: 'I am your Lord,' and they will say: 'You are our Lord.'' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim (part of a long hadith)). Here we mean Allah's coming as an attribute of action, not His form. It is also reported that the Prophet, ﷺ, said: 'Allah will grasp the earth on the Day of Resurrection and fold up the heavens with His right hand, then He will say: 'I am the King!'' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). It is also reported that the Prophet, ﷺ, said: 'When Allah created the creation, He wrote with His hand upon Himself: 'Indeed, My mercy prevails over My wrath.'' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim, At-Tirmidhi). In the hadith about the argument between Adam and Musa, it is reported that the Prophet, ﷺ, said: 'Adam said: 'O Musa, Allah chose you with His word and wrote the Torah for you with His hand.'' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). The speech of the Most High and His hand are essential attributes, His utterance of words is both an essential attribute and an attribute of action, while His writing of the Torah is an attribute of action. It is also reported that the Prophet, ﷺ, said: 'Indeed, Allah extends His hand at night so that the sinner of the day may repent, and He extends His hand during the day so that the sinner of the night may repent.' (Muslim, Ahmad). Many other hadiths of this kind are known.
short_answer: Descending, Coming, Writing, Extending the hand.

question: Are the Most Beautiful Names derived from all attributes of action, or are all names of Allah known only from divine revelation?
answer: No, all names of Allah the Most High are known only from divine revelation, and He should only be called by what He has named Himself in His Book, or by what His Messenger, ﷺ, has called Him. As for the actions of Allah the Most High that He mentions, each of them is connected to praise and indicates perfection. However, not everything with which Allah characterizes Himself can be used as a name, and not every such characteristic can give rise to a name. On the other hand, among the aforementioned characteristics, there are those that can be used as names. For example, Allah the Most High said: 'It is Allah who created you, then provided for you, then will cause you to die, and then will give you life.' (Ar-Rum, 40). And He indeed called Himself the Creator, the Provider, the Life-Giver, the Death-Causer, and the Manager. At the same time, among the actions of Allah mentioned by Him, there are those that were done as recompense and which, in that specific context, are praiseworthy and indicate perfection. For example, Allah the Most High said: 'Indeed, the hypocrites [think to] deceive Allah, but He is deceiving them.' (An-Nisa, 142). 'And they [i.e., the disbelievers] planned, and Allah planned. And Allah is the best of planners.' (Ali 'Imran, 54). Allah the Most High also said: 'They have forgotten Allah, so He has forgotten them.' (At-Tawbah, 67). However, applying the aforementioned attributes of action to Allah outside the context of the relevant verses is impermissible. For example, one should not say that the Most High employs deceit, deceives, mocks, or does anything similar. Likewise, it is impermissible to call Him a deceiver, a plotter, or a mocker, and no Muslim or reasonable person would ever say such a thing, for Allah the Almighty and Majestic did not characterize Himself with concepts like deceit, plotting, or deception except when speaking about retribution against people who wrongfully resorted to such things. Moreover, it is known that just retribution for such actions is considered a good deed even from a created being, so what about the All-Knowing, Just, and Wise Creator!
short_answer: No, names are only from revelation. Not every action is a name.

question: What do such names of the Most High as the Most High (Al-'Ali) and the Highest (Al-A'la) encompass, and what is their relation to the meaning of such names as the Manifest (Az-Zahir), the Subduer (Al-Qahir), and the Exalted (Al-Muta'ali)?
answer: Names such as the Most High and the Highest include an indication of the attribute from which they are derived. In other words, they contain an indication of the circumstance that Allah the Almighty and Majestic, in all respects, occupies the highest position ('uluww). For example, the Most High is above His Throne, and He is above all His creatures. He is separate from them and observes them, knowing what happens to them, possessing such complete knowledge of everything that nothing can be hidden from Him. And He is above everything in the sense that He subdues everything to Himself, and no one can overcome Him, rival Him, oppose Him, or hinder Him. Everything submits to His grandeur, bows before His might, and obeys His majesty, and everything is at His disposal and under His subjugation, unable to free itself from His authority. And He is above everything in that the Almighty, the Great, the All-Good, and the Most High possesses all attributes of perfection, which precludes the possibility of Him having any deficiencies. All aspects of the aforementioned concept of being above everything else are interconnected and inseparable from each other.
short_answer: Exaltation in Essence, status, and power.

question: Which Quranic verses indicate that Allah is above His creation?
answer: There are numerous clear indications of this, among them are the aforementioned names in all their multi-faceted meanings. Examples of such indications are the words of Allah the Most High: 'The Most Merciful [who is] above the Throne established.' (Ta-Ha, 5). This is mentioned in seven verses of the Quran. 'Do you feel secure that He who [holds authority] in the heaven would not cause the earth to swallow you and suddenly it would sway? Or do you feel secure that He who [holds authority] in the heaven would not send against you a storm of stones? Then you would know how [severe] was My warning.' (Al-Mulk, 16-17). This is mentioned in two verses. 'They fear their Lord above them...' (An-Nahl, 50). 'To Him ascends good speech, and righteous work raises it.' (Fatir, 10). 'The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him...' (Al-Ma'arij, 4). 'He arranges [each] matter from the heaven to the earth...' (As-Sajdah, 5). Allah the Most High also said: '[Mention] when Allah said, "O Jesus, indeed I will take you and raise you to Myself..."' (Ali 'Imran, 55). There are other indications of this kind in the Quran.
short_answer: Numerous verses about the establishment over the Throne and being above.
source: Ta-Ha, 5; Al-Mulk, 16-17; An-Nahl, 50; Fatir, 10; Al-Ma'arij, 4; As-Sajdah, 5; Ali 'Imran, 55

question: Are there indications of this kind in the Sunnah?
answer: There are numerous indications of this in the Sunnah. In the hadith about the siege of the Banu Qurayzah, it is reported that the Prophet, ﷺ, said to Sa'd: 'You have judged them with the judgment of the Sovereign who is above the seven heavens.' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim, Ahmad). In another hadith, it is reported that once the Prophet, ﷺ, asked a young slave girl: 'Where is Allah?' and when she replied, 'In the heaven,' he said to her master: 'Set her free, for indeed she is a believer.' (Muslim, Ahmad). The same is indicated by the content of the hadiths about the Prophet's ascension (Mi'raj) and his words in the hadith about the successive angels: 'Then those angels who stayed with you during the night ascend, and He asks them, though He knows best (about the affairs of the people).' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). It is also reported that the Prophet, ﷺ, said: 'Whoever gives charity equal to a date from good (halal) earnings - and Allah accepts only the good - ...' (Al-Bukhari, Muslim). In the hadith about revelations, the Prophet, ﷺ, said: 'When Allah decrees a matter in the heaven, the angels flutter their wings in submission to His words, (and a sound is heard) like a chain being dragged over a rock.' (Al-Bukhari, At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah - part of a long hadith). Many other examples could be cited which indicate what the vast majority of scholars agree upon.
short_answer: Hadiths about the slave girl, the ascension, and Sa'd's judgment.
source: Al-Bukhari, Muslim, Ahmad, At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah

question: What did the Imams of the religion from among our righteous predecessors (Salaf) say about the establishment (Istiwa') of Allah over His Throne?
answer: All of them, may Allah the Most High have mercy on them, said that the Istiwa' is not unknown (i.e., its occurrence is affirmed), but its modality is incomprehensible; belief in it is obligatory; inquiring about it is an innovation; the message is from Allah; the Messenger was obliged to convey it; and it is necessary for us to affirm and submit. They said the same regarding all other verses and hadiths concerning the names and attributes of Allah. Allah the Most High said that those firmly grounded in knowledge say: 'We believe in it; all [of it] is from our Lord...' (Ali 'Imran, 7). And Allah the Most High informed that the disciples of 'Isa, peace be upon him, said: 'We have believed in Allah, and bear witness that we are Muslims [in submission to Him].' (Ali 'Imran, 52).
short_answer: Istiwa' is known, its modality is unknown, belief is obligatory, questioning is a bid'ah.

question: Which Quranic verses indicate that Allah is the All-Subduer?
answer: There are many such indications. For example, Allah the Most High said: '...And He is the Prevailing over His servants...' (Al-An'am, 18). These words contain an indication that Allah the Most High is the All-Subduer and that He is above all. Allah the Most High also said: 'Exalted is He, He is Allah, the One, the Prevailing.' (Az-Zumar, 4). 'To whom belongs [all] sovereignty that Day? To Allah, the One, the Prevailing.' (Ghafir, 16). 'Say, "I am only a warner, and there is no deity except Allah, the One, the Prevailing."' (Sad, 65). 'And there is no creature on earth but that upon Allah is its provision...' (Hud, 56). 'O company of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass. You will not pass except by authority [from Allah].' (Ar-Rahman, 33). Other verses can serve as examples of such indications.
short_answer: Verses with the name Al-Qahhar and about authority over all existence.
source: Al-An'am, 18; Az-Zumar, 4; Ghafir, 16; Sad, 65; Hud, 56; Ar-Rahman, 33

question: Which hadiths indicate that Allah is the All-Subduer?
answer: There are many such indications in the Sunnah. For example, it is reported that when supplicating before sleeping, the Prophet, ﷺ, would say: 'I seek refuge in You from the evil of everything You have control over.' (Abu Dawud). And it is reported that when supplicating in times of distress and sorrow, the Prophet, ﷺ, would say: 'O Allah, indeed I am Your servant, son of Your male servant, son of Your female servant. I am under Your control, Your rulings over me are binding, and the decree You have passed concerning me is just.' (Ahmad). It is also reported that when supplicating during the night prayers, the Prophet, ﷺ, would say: 'Indeed, You judge, and no one can judge You. Indeed, he whom You support is never humiliated, and he whom You oppose is never honored.' (An-Nasa'i, At-Tirmidhi). Many other examples could be cited.
short_answer: The Prophet's supplications about complete submission to Allah.

question: What testifies to the loftiness of Allah the Almighty and Majestic, and what must be negated concerning Him?
answer: Know that the loftiness of Allah is indicated by what is implied by His names such as the Holy (Al-Quddus), the Peace (As-Salam), the Great (Al-Kabir), and the Exalted (Al-Muta'ali) in all their multifaceted meanings, and by what necessarily follows from His possession of attributes of perfection and majesty. In His oneness, He is far above having anyone share His authority even partially, or having anyone assist Him, or having an intercessor before Him without His permission, or having a protector. In His greatness, grandeur, absolute authority, and might, He is far above anyone rivaling Him, overcoming Him, protecting Him from humiliation, or aiding Him. In His eternity, He is far above having a spouse, a child, a father, an equal, or a likeness. In His perfection, life, eternal existence, and power, He is far above death, drowsiness, sleep, fatigue, or weariness. Possessing perfect knowledge, He is far above negligence, forgetfulness, or being unaware of any atom's weight on earth or in the heavens. Possessing perfect wisdom, He is far above creating anything in play, or leaving what He created to itself without commanding and prohibiting His creation, or not resurrecting people, leaving them without recompense. In the perfection of His justice, He is far above wronging anyone in the least or not fully rewarding a person for good deeds. Being absolutely free of need, He is far above being fed or provided for. Possessing all those qualities by which He characterized Himself or by which His Messenger characterized Him, He is far above both denial (of His attributes) and likening Him to anyone. Glory and praise be to the Almighty and Majestic, the All-Good and Most High, who has nothing in common with what is incompatible with His divinity, His lordship, His Most Beautiful Names, and His Lofty Attributes, for Allah the Most High said: 'He presents an example for you from yourselves. Do you have among those whom your right hands possess any partners in what We have provided for you so that you are equal therein [and] would fear them as your fear of one another [within a partnership]? Thus do We detail the verses for a people who use reason.' (Ar-Rum, 28). The relevant verses of the Quran and hadiths of the Prophet's Sunnah are well-known, perfectly clear, and numerous.
short_answer: Attributes of Majesty. Negation of deficiencies (death, sleep, offspring, need).

question: What is the meaning of the Prophet's words, ﷺ, about the Most Beautiful Names: '...will enter Paradise whoever enumerates them'?
answer: These words have been interpreted in various ways. For example, they mean that all the names of Allah should be memorized, and that one should supplicate to Allah and praise Him using them. They also mean that a servant of Allah should accustom himself to what these names indicate and to what it is permissible to emulate, striving, for instance, to be merciful and compassionate, provided that the servant can indeed possess such qualities to the best of his ability. As for such attributes of Allah as the Compeller (Al-Jabbar), the Great (Al-'Azim), or the Exalted (Al-Mutakabbir), the servant should acknowledge them, humble himself before them, and not attempt to adorn himself with any such attributes. As for attributes related to promise, examples of which are names like the Forgiving (Al-Ghafur), the Appreciative (Ash-Shakur), the Pardoner (Al-'Afu), the Kind (Ar-Ra'uf), the Forbearing (Al-Halim), the Generous (Al-Jawad), and the Noble (Al-Karim), the servant should limit himself to hope and aspiration. Finally, as for attributes of Allah related to threat, examples of which are names like the Almighty (Al-'Aziz), the Possessor of Retribution (Dhu Intiqam), Severe in Punishment (Shadid al-'Iqab), or Swift in Account (Sari' al-Hisab), the servant should limit himself to fear. The Prophet's words, ﷺ, indicate that the servant should bear witness to the truth of the meaning of these names and give them their due right, knowing them and acting as a servant should. An example is one who testifies that Allah the Most High is above His creation and exalted over them, that He established Himself over His Throne, being separate from His creatures while at the same time having full knowledge of them and extending His power over them, etc. Such a person worships Allah in accordance with this quality of the Most High, which leads to a yearning for Allah in his heart, and he begins to have secret conversations with Him, lowering his gaze and standing before Him like a submissive servant stands before a mighty ruler, feeling that all his words and deeds ascend to Him and are presented to Him, and thus feeling ashamed to say or do anything that, reaching those lofty realms, would disgrace him.
